data.body:
LANDED. Change 1646 submitted and MERGED; on Gerrit main as 54bdc0f8af (Gerrit rebased server-side on submit, so the landed sha differs from the pushed one). Both gates were green before submit: LLM-Review +1 (rebar-review-bot) and Verified +1 (rebar-ci-bot). Change 1641 is ABANDONED with a message pointing at 1646.

All 13 acceptance criteria verified against the LANDED tree (worktree reset to 54bdc0f8af, not the local pre-rebase commit): 19 tests in the new file pass, 514 tests across the apply + diffing suites pass, make lint and make typecheck both exit 0.

What the fix does, in one line: an inbound link ADD whose failure is a deterministic verdict about the local graph is attempted once, recorded durably with a digest over the inputs that decided it, and skipped thereafter until those inputs change.

Expected effect on the live bridge: the 19 doomed rebar.link writes per pass drop to 0 in steady state, and the permanent WARNING floor drains to a single INFO summary line. Worth watching the next few Reconcile Bridge runs to confirm the drop empirically — the record only takes effect once a pass has run with the new code AND committed impossible_links.json to the tickets branch, so expect one more pass at 19 attempts (which writes the records) before the count falls.

Honest residuals, recorded rather than hidden:
- The differ still EMITS these ADD records every pass; the fix suppresses the write, not the record. Emitting is cheap; suppressing at the differ would have meant touching the G3/G4/G5 suppression surface that epic despotic-floriated-leopard owns, so it was deliberately left alone.
- A cycle record keys on the global structural projection, so any structural change anywhere in the store re-qualifies it for one attempt. That is the deliberate safe direction: over-invalidating costs one write, under-invalidating would suppress a legitimate link indefinitely.
